clue.text: Material from forecaster easily deluded one

parts.note: a seer is a prophet who foretells the future
a sucker is a gullible person, easily taken in

explanation.surface: A fabric somehow sold by a fortune-teller to a gullible customer.
explanation.definitionFit: Seersucker is a puckered cotton fabric, so it is a kind of material.

clue.text: Special cat in prominent story

parts.note: the cat-o'-nine-tails is a whip, so a cat gives a lash

explanation.surface: A remarkable cat featured as a newspaper's front-page story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cat' suggests a pet; here it is the whip.
explanation.definitionFit: A splash is a front-page newspaper story given prominent display.

clue.text: Legislator in Ireland's realm

indicators.note: the legislator is placed inside the name of the country

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland
an MP, Member of Parliament, makes laws

explanation.surface: A lawmaker working within the Irish kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: An empire is a domain ruled by one sovereign, a realm.

clue.text: Avionics tester deployed source of fuel

indicators.note: things deployed are spread out and arranged anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An aircraft electronics inspector sent out to find somewhere to refuel.
explanation.definitionFit: A service station is a roadside place selling petrol, so a source of fuel.

clue.text: Dish with crust covering small part

indicators.note: a covering goes round something, so the crust's letters enclose the small letter

parts.note: a case is an outer shell or crust, as of pastry
a role is an acting part

explanation.surface: A dish where pastry covers only a small part of the filling.
explanation.definitionFit: A casserole is a stewed dish cooked slowly in the oven.

clue.text: Short form of rugby fails to start with equal chance

indicators.note: failing to start means the opening letter goes missing

parts.note: sevens is a short, seven-a-side version of rugby

explanation.surface: A rugby match that won't kick off leaves the outcome a toss-up.
explanation.definitionFit: In betting, evens means a fifty-fifty chance, odds of one to one.

clue.text: Special forces will absorb pressure in healthy places

indicators.note: to absorb something is to take it inside, so the forces' letters wrap round the pressure letter

parts.note: the SAS is Britain's Special Air Service regiment
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Elite troops taking the strain while recovering in health resorts.
explanation.definitionFit: Spa towns are resorts visited for their health-giving waters.

clue.text: Cadet pin moulded by purist

definitions.note: a noun in the clue standing for an adjective: pedantic is what a purist is

indicators.note: something moulded is reshaped, so the letters take a new form

explanation.surface: A military cadet's badge shaped by a perfectionist.
explanation.definitionFit: A purist insists on strict correctness, which is the fussy, over-precise attitude described.

clue.text: Cheap way to travel always used in acting profession

indicators.note: the poetic word is placed inside the word for acting profession

parts.note: the stage stands for the theatrical profession
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: Touring actors always travelling on the cheap.
explanation.definitionFit: Steerage was the cheapest class of passage on a ship.

clue.text: Tom, Dick or Harry entertains them crazily

indicators.note: crazily signals letters jumbled in a wild way

explanation.surface: An ordinary fellow putting on a mad show for his guests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom, Dick or Harry' names any ordinary person; 'entertains' looks like the link but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Any Tom, Dick or Harry is an ordinary person, the typical citizen.

clue.text: This outcast returns to drive back

indicators.note: something that returns goes back the way it came, so the synonym is read from right to left

parts.note: to repel is to drive back an attacker

explanation.surface: A shunned figure coming back to fight off attackers.
explanation.definitionFit: A leper, shunned for the disease, became the standard word for a social outcast.

clue.text: King Edward on horseback apparently to take flight

indicators.note: a rider sits on horseback in the saddle, so the royal letters go inside the seat

parts.note: the saddle is where one sits on horseback
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
Ed is the short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A monarch on his horse seeming to bolt from the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apparently' admits that the saddle stands loosely for 'horseback'.
explanation.definitionFit: To skedaddle is informal for running away hurriedly, much like fleeing.

clue.text: A diner's chewed fish

indicators.note: food that is chewed is broken up and mixed about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive is read as plain diners, keeping the S

explanation.surface: A restaurant customer's mouthful of small fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The sardine is a small oily fish of the herring family.

clue.text: Sort of bowler hat of staff by London suburb

indicators.note: a hat sits on top, so only the opening letter of the word is taken

parts.note: Pinner is a suburb in north-west London

explanation.surface: A bowler hat worn by a member of staff from the outskirts of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowler' and 'hat' suggest headwear, but the bowler is a cricketer who spins the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a spinner is a bowler who imparts spin, so it is one type of bowler.

clue.text: Scoring tends to be messed up by these inferior players

indicators.note: something messed up is thrown into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A team's scoring tends to suffer because of its weaker members.
explanation.definitionFit: The second string is the reserve team, players below first-choice standard.

clue.text: He does painting etc, 20th-century art style, Art Nouveau, and alternative

parts.note: Art Deco was a decorative style of the 1920s and 30s

indicators.note: nouveau is French for new, so the word is made new by rearranging it

parts.note: or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A tradesman who paints, listing art styles from Deco to Nouveau.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art Nouveau' looks like the art movement; it is RAT, a new form of ART.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorator paints and papers rooms, so is a house painter by trade.

clue.text: Start coach out of spectators' sight

parts.note: the off is the start of a race
a stage is a stagecoach

explanation.surface: The first stage of a coach journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Offstage means out of the audience's view, in the wings.

clue.text: He spoke philosophically of very dilapidated cars

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
crates is slang for old, broken-down cars

explanation.surface: A man musing deeply about old bangers.
explanation.definitionFit: Socrates was the Athenian philosopher known for his spoken dialogues.

clue.text: Leading politician from France taking on consumption with little hesitation

indicators.note: taking means holding something within, so the French word wraps the next letters

parts.note: something from France is French
taken as written
TB, tuberculosis, was formerly called consumption
er is the short sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A senior French politician eating and drinking while hesitating briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: Front-benchers are ministers or shadow ministers who sit at the front in Parliament, hence leading politicians.

clue.text: Beetle sacred to some, namely Egyptian etc

parts.note: sc, from scilicet, is the abbreviation for namely
an Egyptian is one example of an Arab

explanation.surface: An insect revered by ancient Egyptians.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarab beetle was sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: A bishop perhaps for every one

parts.note: a bishop is a chess piece

explanation.surface: A clergyman serving every member of the flock.
explanation.definitionFit: Apiece means each, so for every one.

clue.text: Heartless Scot to strain some porridge

indicators.note: with its heart gone, the word keeps only its first and last letters

parts.note: to retch is to strain as if vomiting

explanation.surface: A Scotsman gagging on a bowl of oats.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang 'porridge' means time served in prison, and a stretch is a prison sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch is a term of imprisonment, which is what porridge means in British slang.

clue.text: Moor yacht — that was his hobby

definitions.meaning: a moor is open uncultivated upland
Edward ..., UK prime minister, was a keen ocean-racing yachtsman

explanation.definitionFit: A heath is open moorland, and Edward Heath was the sailing prime minister.

clue.text: An investigator in charge to limit tax

indicators.note: the investigator and article are placed inside the word for charge

parts.note: a rap is a criminal charge, as in beat the rap
an gives the article A
tec is short for detective

explanation.surface: A detective in charge of controlling taxes.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate-cap was to impose a government ceiling on local council rates, a property tax.

clue.text: He could be trained by NASA tutor

indicators.note: a body that is trained is reshaped, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A space agency instructor preparing a recruit for a mission.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronaut is a space traveller, the sort of man NASA would train.

clue.text: Spooky European lake

parts.note: Erie is one of North America's Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A haunted lake somewhere in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie and spooky are synonyms for strange and frightening.

clue.text: Bridge player, champ, taking in one of his opponents

indicators.note: taking in means enclosing, so the verb wraps around the opponent's letter

parts.note: to champ is to chew noisily, to eat
at bridge, ... plays against North and South; S is South

explanation.surface: A bridge player and champion facing one of his rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge the four players are named by compass point, and one of them sits at this one.

clue.text: Kind of daily independent chart

parts.note: a daily or char is a British cleaning lady who comes in each day
a table is a chart of figures

explanation.surface: A sort of newspaper chart from an independent daily paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daily' suggests a newspaper; here it is a cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: Charitable means generous and kind towards others.
